entries.name: Weeping willow
entries.leaves: deciduous, long narrow, golden in autumn
entries.flowers: yellow catkins, spring with the leaves
entries.voxel_shape: rounded crown of long hanging branches that touch the water
entries.notes: The archetypal riverside tree; in the game its drooping boughs should overhang the water. Needs wet roots, so plant it at the waterline.

entries.name: White willow
entries.leaves: deciduous, silvery-green beneath
entries.flowers: slim yellow catkins, spring
entries.voxel_shape: tall broad crown, trunk furrows into rough diamond pattern
entries.notes: The bat wood of cricket; willow bark is the original source of salicin, the aspirin precursor. Loves floodplain soils.

entries.name: Black willow
entries.leaves: deciduous, narrow lanceolate
entries.flowers: greenish catkins, spring
entries.voxel_shape: irregular leaning crown often divided into several trunks
entries.notes: North America's largest native willow; first tree to colonize fresh sandbars and gravel banks after floods.

entries.name: Black alder
entries.leaves: deciduous, rounded with a notched tip
entries.flowers: long male catkins and small woody female cones
entries.fruit: tiny winged nuts from woody cones
entries.voxel_shape: pyramidal dark crown, often standing in shallow water
entries.notes: Fixes nitrogen via Frankia root nodules like a legume; one of the few trees happy standing in water.

entries.name: Black poplar
entries.leaves: deciduous, diamond-shaped on long flattened stalks
entries.flowers: red male and green female catkins, wind-pollinated, spring
entries.voxel_shape: massive rugged trunk with a broad irregular crown
entries.notes: The old river-meadow giant; its cotton-fluff seeds drift down rivers every June. Now rare on engineered banks.

entries.name: River birch
entries.leaves: deciduous, triangular with doubly toothed edges
entries.flowers: slender catkins, spring
entries.voxel_shape: peeling salmon-pink bark, oval crown, often leaning over water
entries.notes: Peeling cinnamon bark is unmistakable; the most flood-tolerant of the birches and often multi-trunked.

entries.name: Bald cypress
entries.leaves: deciduous conifer, soft feathery needles that rust and drop in autumn
entries.flowers: inconspicuous; small globular female cones
entries.voxel_shape: flared buttress trunk with 'knees' poking from the water, spire-like crown
entries.notes: The swamp sentinel: stands for centuries in water, growing hollow 'knees' at the surface. Its heartwood does not rot.

entries.name: River red gum
entries.leaves: evergreen, long grey-green lanceolate
entries.flowers: cream-white massed stamens, summer
entries.voxel_shape: towering fluted trunk, smooth white-to-red patchy bark, sparse crown
entries.notes: Australia's signature river tree; deciduous strips of bark peel in summer and floods leave it standing when other trees drown.

entries.name: American sycamore
entries.leaves: deciduous, huge maple-like lobed, fuzzy beneath
entries.flowers: ball-shaped heads, inconspicuous, spring
entries.fruit: dangling brown balls of tufted achenes
entries.voxel_shape: massive trunk with white and olive camouflage-flaking bark
entries.notes: Called a 'buttonwood' for its fruit balls; the camouflage bark high above the flood line is the easiest ID from a boat.

entries.name: Fremont's cottonwood
entries.leaves: deciduous, heart-shaped, gold in autumn
entries.flowers: catkins, wind-pollinated, very early spring
entries.fruit: capsules releasing fluffy snow-like seed blizzards
entries.voxel_shape: tall broad crown, deep furrows, sticky buds
entries.notes: The green ribbon along western US rivers; without it a desert river is just a dry wash most of the year.

entries.name: Elder
entries.leaves: deciduous, pinnate, elderflower smell when crushed
entries.flowers: flat cream corymbs, early summer
entries.fruit: glossy black-purple berries in drooping heads
entries.voxel_shape: hollow-pithed soft woody shrub with flat white umbels
entries.notes: Famous in country medicine; raw berries are mildly toxic, always cook them. Hollow stems make natural whistles.

entries.name: Goat willow
entries.leaves: deciduous, oval, downy beneath
entries.flowers: fat silky catkins (pussy willows), late winter
entries.voxel_shape: bushy grey shrub, first to flower in late winter
entries.notes: 'Pussy willow'; its catkins are the first reliable nectar of the year and feed queen bumblebees waking from hibernation.

entries.name: Saltcedar
entries.leaves: evergreen to semi-evergreen, tiny scale-like
entries.flowers: pink feathery plumes, summer
entries.voxel_shape: feathery pink-green thicket hugging dry riverbeds
entries.notes: Exotic invader across the western US and Australia: deep roots drain the water table and excrete salt, sterilizing the soil.

entries.name: Common reed
entries.leaves: perennial grass, broad floppy blades, spreads by rhizome
entries.flowers: large feathery purple-grey panicles, late summer
entries.voxel_shape: dense vertical reedbeds with plumed heads rippling in wind
entries.notes: The thatch on old European roofs and the reedbeds that filter sewage; forms monocultural stands that can run for hectares.

entries.name: Broadleaf cattail
entries.leaves: perennial, long flat straps from rhizome
entries.flowers: brown sausage spike of female flowers under a yellow male spike
entries.voxel_shape: stiff vertical blades topped by brown hot-dog spikes
uses: edible rhizomes and shoots ('supermarket of the swamp')
entries.notes: Nearly every part is edible; the brown spikes split open in late summer into snow-like fluff that flies on any breeze.

entries.name: Common club-rush
entries.leaves: semi-evergreen sedge, leafless round green stems (bulrushes)
entries.flowers: brownish spikelets near the stem tip
entries.voxel_shape: dense stands of round upright dark-green spears
entries.notes: The classic European weaving rush; strong round stems cut in summer dry to pale straw for mats and chair seats.

entries.name: Giant reed
entries.leaves: evergreen, broad arching blades on cane-like stems
entries.flowers: large feathery silvery panicles, autumn
entries.voxel_shape: tall dense canefields, green-blue blades arching over
entries.notes: Clarinet and sax reeds come from this grass. Severely invasive in warm rivers worldwide; do not plant without control.

entries.name: Papyrus
entries.leaves: perennial sedge, leafless triangular stem topped by a green starburst
entries.flowers: small brown umbels within the tuft
entries.voxel_shape: tall smooth triangular canes with firework-like green heads
entries.notes: The paper of Egypt for three millennia; wild Cyperus-papyrus swamps still fringe the Nile and central African lakes.

entries.name: Water horsetail
entries.leaves: spore-bearing, jointed hollow stems with black-toothed sheaths, no true leaves
entries.flowers: none (spore cones at stem tips)
entries.voxel_shape: whorled vertical reed canes, airy and jointed
entries.notes: A living fossil older than the dinosaurs; stems are stiff with silica and were used to scrub pots and brass.

entries.name: Yellow flag iris
entries.leaves: perennial, sword-like in two ranks from a fleshy rhizome
entries.flowers: bright yellow with darker veining, late spring
entries.voxel_shape: arching fan of sword leaves, bold yellow standard flowers
entries.notes: Every part, especially the rhizome, is toxic; it is also a serious invasive outside Europe, clogging North American wetlands.

entries.name: Common water plantain
entries.leaves: perennial, broad oval on long stalks (emergent or floating)
entries.flowers: small white to pink flowers in open whorls on a tall stem
entries.voxel_shape: rosette of broad ovals, tall open candelabra of tiny blossom
entries.notes: The open branched spike of stars above the water is the easiest ID; raw tubers irritate, so treat before eating.

entries.name: Water mint
entries.leaves: perennial, toothed, strongly minty when crushed
entries.flowers: lilac head-like whorls, summer
entries.voxel_shape: low sprawling mat of round-toothed leaves and lilac pom-pom flowers
entries.notes: The mint of English riversides; one of the parents of spearmint, and a summer magnet for bees and hoverflies.

entries.name: Branched bur-reed
entries.leaves: perennial, strap-like in two ranks from creeping rhizome
entries.flowers: male spikes above, female spiky spheres below on a branched stem
entries.fruit: hard bur-like nutlets in spiky balls
entries.voxel_shape: starburst of green spikes, green-black spiky balls on side branches
entries.notes: The spiky double-decker fruit balls are unmistakable and take years to rot; herons love the shallow shelves it forms.

entries.name: Greater pond sedge
entries.leaves: perennial, broad stiff blue-green blades from short stout rhizome
entries.flowers: green-brown spikes, late spring
entries.voxel_shape: dense tussocks of stiff sedge on the water's edge
entries.notes: One of the biggest and showiest sedges; an architect of the British river margin, binding soft banks against wash.

entries.name: Reed canary grass
entries.leaves: perennial, broad ribbed blades, rhizomatous
entries.flowers: panicles flushed purple-green maturing to beige
entries.voxel_shape: tall dense grass stands with plumed purple-green heads
entries.notes: Native to Eurasia but a notorious choking invader in North American wetlands; its roots pull nitrates out of farm runoff.

entries.name: Watercress
entries.leaves: evergreen perennial, pinnate, peppery
entries.flowers: small white four-petaled, spring
entries.voxel_shape: trailing mats of dark pinnate leaves sprawling on cool running water
entries.notes: Cool limy streams only; the peppery leaf of the classic Victorian sandwich. Wild cress can carry liver fluke, wash before eating.

entries.name: Purple loosestrife
entries.leaves: perennial, lanceolate on square stems, hairy
entries.flowers: tall dense magenta spikes, midsummer
entries.voxel_shape: column of magenta flower spikes above willow-herb foliage
entries.notes: Stunning in bloom and feared in America, where it has swallowed wetlands; imported beetles now fight it biologically.

entries.name: Arrowhead
entries.leaves: perennial, arrow-shaped emergent blades on long stalks
entries.flowers: white three-petaled in whorls, summer
entries.voxel_shape: rosette of emergent arrow leaves, white flowers three petals at a time
entries.notes: Underground tubers fed foragers and ducks for millennia; the arrow-shaped emergent leaves are instantly recognizable.

entries.name: White water lily
entries.leaves: perennial, large floating round pads with a V-notch
entries.flowers: fragrant white floating star, summer midday
entries.voxel_shape: floating pads scattered with white stars on slow water
entries.notes: Monet's subject; flowers open at midday and close by teatime, and the rhizomes were nibbled in famine times.

entries.name: Sacred lotus
entries.leaves: perennial, huge round emergent leaves that shed water (lotus effect)
entries.flowers: pink or white emergent bowls, summer dawn
entries.fruit: showerhead seed pod (iconic), seeds viable for centuries
entries.voxel_shape: emergent round blue-waxy parasols above the surface, pink lotuses
uses: edible rhizomes, seeds and young leaves
entries.notes: Seeds have germinated after a thousand years in dry storage; leaves sit higher above water than water lilies and shed every drop.

entries.name: Giant Amazon water lily
entries.leaves: annual-perennial, enormous floating pads to 2.5-3 m across, upturned rims
entries.flowers: night-blooming, white turning pink over two nights, fragrant
entries.voxel_shape: gigantic lily pads with upturned edges, huge pink-white night blooms
entries.notes: Leaves hold 40+ kg without sinking; the flower opens white at night, blushes pink by dawn and never opens the same way twice.

entries.name: Common duckweed
entries.leaves: perennial, tiny ovals floating free, no true roots structure complexity
entries.flowers: inconspicuous, rarely seen
entries.voxel_shape: green film of seed-like dots carpeting still backwaters
entries.notes: One of the smallest flowering plants and the fastest-growing: a duckweed mat can double in two days and strip nitrogen from wastewater.

entries.name: Water hyacinth
entries.leaves: perennial, glossy round leaves on swollen spongy stalks
entries.flowers: lavender spikes with a yellow-blue blotch, year-round
entries.voxel_shape: floating rosettes with purple spikes, inflating rafts that block rivers
entries.notes: Often called the world's worst aquatic weed: one plant becomes a mother of millions, jamming Nile and Congo waterways solid.

entries.name: Water lettuce
entries.leaves: perennial, velvety ribbed rosettes, spongy floating base
entries.flowers: tiny white, inconspicuous, hidden in the rosette
entries.voxel_shape: floating pale-green lettuce rosettes drifting in rafts
entries.notes: Floats like lettuce but chokes tropical rivers; spreads mostly by daughter rosettes pinching off, not by seed.

entries.name: European frogbit
entries.leaves: perennial, small heart-shaped floating pads
entries.flowers: white three-petaled with a yellow base, summer
entries.voxel_shape: small frogbit hearts scattered on calm shallows
entries.notes: The mini-lily of backwaters; escaped in North America and now listed as invasive in some states.

entries.name: Water caltrop
entries.leaves: annual, floating rosette with inflated spongy stalk midribs
entries.flowers: inconspicuous greenish-white, above the rosette
entries.fruit: woody horned 'caltrop' nuts, edible, treacherous underfoot for swimmers
entries.voxel_shape: floating horn-nut rosettes carpeting slow water
entries.notes: Its nuts shredded swimmers' feet so badly that laws were passed against it in America; yet it is a prized snack across Asia.

entries.name: Floating-leaved pondweed
entries.leaves: perennial, oval floating leaves with leathery green leathery pads and long submerged leaves
entries.flowers: emergent spike of tiny greenish flowers, summer
entries.voxel_shape: patch of flat oval pond-leaves with emergent bottle-brush spikes
entries.notes: The backbone of fish life in slow rivers: every fry hides under these pads and every duck grazes the stalks.

entries.name: Canadian waterweed
entries.leaves: evergreen perennial, dark green whorls of three along the stem
entries.flowers: tiny white at the surface, dioecious
entries.voxel_shape: green underwater forests of whorled stems; oxygen bubbles on sunny days
entries.notes: Escaped from North America and once choked English canals so completely that boats could not pass; still the aquarium classic.
